source.title: On the Stability Properties and the Optimization Landscape of Training Problems with Squared Loss for Neural Networks and General Nonlinear Conic Approximation Schemes

record.tranche_reason: The paper proves theoretical results about squared-loss optimization landscapes, but does not test the listed versions’ training outcomes, initialization, width effects, or training recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper’s proofs and corollaries establish existence of spurious minima and non-optimal stationary points for certain label vectors. These do not report gradient-based training outcomes or the listed version-specific behaviors. Numerical results cited from other work are not this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study proves conditional existence and instability results for squared-loss landscapes. It does not establish gradient-descent convergence frequencies, teacher-student width effects, classification training error, or the initialization and training-recipe comparisons named in V1–V6. Existence of spurious minima, including in realizable networks, does not establish that standard initialization and gradient training encounter them.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: under the paper's assumptions, improved expressiveness of nonlinear conic approximation schemes is quantitatively linked to instability and bad stationary points for certain labels. Overparameterization and parameter-size regularization cannot generally eliminate all these problems. The author acknowledges strong practical SGD performance and leaves probabilistic explanations of optimizer behavior for future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper gives an axiomatic mathematical analysis of squared-loss landscapes and proves existence results; it does not run the benchmark training recipes in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Theoretical conclusions depend on expressiveness and conicity assumptions, label realizability, activation-function properties, widths, and sample-count conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the stated architecture and data assumptions, squared-loss neural-network problems have arbitrarily bad spurious local minima for an open cone of labels; in the realizable case, Corollary 47 covers every label vector that is not affine-linearly fittable. Under m < n·dy, every differentiability point is a non-optimal stationary point for suitable labels.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Conditional squared-loss landscape results establish the existence of bad stationary points, even in some realizable networks, without determining whether gradient training from standard initialization reaches them.

record.problems: The relevant evidence is theoretical and conditional on assumptions and selected label vectors; it does not measure optimizer convergence, initialization effects, benchmark training errors, or how often the constructed conditions occur in practice.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible version-specific training-result rows are reported. Cited numerical findings from other work are excluded.

untested.parts: CIFAR classification training error under SGD or Adam, including random labels and model-size, stopping, and regularization comparisons.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student convergence from standard initialization, growth of failure frequency with matched widths, and the benefit of one or two extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, identity-shortcut comparisons, special initialization of plain tanh networks, and normalization-free residual training.
Initialization-dependent signal propagation, training speed, trainable depth, orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparisons, and 10,000-layer convolutional training.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss and curvature trajectories, recovery, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's stability concerns sensitivity of best approximations or solution sets to labels, rather than the learning-rate stability in V5. Its residual-network expressiveness result does not test V3 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR training error, random or corrupted labels, SGD or Adam outcomes, and effects of model size, training duration, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU experiments, gradient descent from standard initialization, and the stated student-to-teacher width comparisons.
Plain versus residual training error by depth, and empirical tests of special initialization or normalization-free residual training.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, training speed, trainable depth, and 10,000-layer convolutional training.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss and curvature trajectories, and divergence outcomes.
Batch-normalization speed and learning-rate tolerance comparisons, and Fixup training outcomes.

rows.subject: deep and shallow neural networks with variable widths and activation functions affine on an open interval
rows.size_stated: variable widths; no specific size stated
rows.operation_detail: Proves existence of spurious local minima for squared-loss training problems under stated architectural and data conditions.

conditions.value: each activation is affine-linear on an open nonempty interval
network satisfies Theorem 39 or Corollary 40 conditions

rows.measure: Existence of a spurious local minimum for each label vector in an open nonempty cone; minima can be arbitrarily bad in relative and absolute terms and in loss.
rows.value: Theorem proves the stated existence result; no numerical value reported.
rows.note: An analytical existence result for selected label vectors and assumptions; it does not show that gradient training from random initialization reaches these minima or that training error remains high.
rows.check: The existence result is correctly reported but cannot determine any listed version's effect. Corollary 47 additionally requires each affine segment to have a non-vanishing derivative; the row omits this condition. Constant segments are treated separately in Corollary 48. The operation is a mathematical proof rather than an empirical measurement.

rows.subject: neural networks satisfying the conditions in Setting 35
rows.operation_detail: Proves that every differentiability point can be a spurious local minimum or saddle point for suitable label vectors.

conditions.value: conditions of Lemma 38, Theorem 39, or Corollary 40

rows.measure: Existence of non-optimal stationary points; they can be arbitrarily bad.
rows.value: Theorem-derived existence statement; no numerical value reported.
rows.note: The result concerns stationary points for appropriately chosen labels, not frequency of convergence from initialization or benchmark training error.
rows.check: Corollary 45 correctly concerns every differentiability point when m < n·dy, with labels chosen for that point. It proves neither convergence to those points nor their frequency under fixed labels and standard initialization. The operation is a mathematical proof rather than an empirical measurement.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
